evals.prompt: plan my week: I want to finish the landing page for my side project, go to the gym 3 times, and read 100 pages of Deep Work. I have about an hour on weekday evenings and 3 hours on Saturday, Sunday is family day.
evals.expected_output: A Monday-to-Sunday plan with 3 goals, each with a concrete done-means; verb-first tasks of 15-90 min; no tasks on Sunday; each day at or under 70% of its capacity (42 min weekdays, 126 Saturday); gym sessions not on consecutive days; a light day; a totals line; no clarifying questions.
assertions: Asks no questions before giving the plan
No weekday has more than 42 planned minutes
Every task is 15 to 90 minutes and starts with a verb
Gym sessions are not on consecutive days
Ends with a totals line and offers to save

evals.prompt: I want to get healthier, learn Spanish, launch my Etsy shop, clean my garage and start journaling this week
evals.expected_output: Asks at most two questions in one message: time available per day, and asks to pick the top 3 of 5 goals (parking the rest in Later) and/or what done means for 'get healthier'. Does not produce a 5-goal plan.
assertions: Asks at most two questions, in a single message
Asks the user to choose 3 goals or proposes parking 2 in a Later list
Does not produce a plan with all 5 goals

evals.prompt:
review my week. Here's what I had:
Mon - [x] Outline blog post (30m) - [x] Run 30m
Tue - [ ] Draft blog post intro (45m)
Wed - [x] Run 30m - [ ] Fix login bug (60m)
Thu - [ ] Draft blog post intro (45m) (already moved once)
Fri - [ ] Run 30m - [ ] Read 30 pages (40m)
I got sick on Thursday.
evals.expected_output: Leads with the numbers (3 done of 7 distinct tasks, or 8 counting the moved one; under 50% either way) and wins first; does not blame; asks the three review questions in one message, skipping 'what got in the way' since illness was given; rolls over the unfinished non-habit tasks, offering shrink/first/drop for the twice-moved blog intro; does not carry the missed run; suggests a smaller next week since completion was under 50%.
assertions: States done count and percentage before anything else
Does not ask what got in the way (the user said they were sick)
Does not carry over the missed run as a task
Offers shrink, schedule first, or drop for the blog intro task
Recommends a smaller plan next week

evals.prompt: what's on today? I already did the run btw
evals.expected_output: Loads the current week from the dashboard or asks for the pasted list if neither exists; marks the run done; lists today's remaining tasks and up to 3 overdue ones with an offer to move them; short reply.
assertions: Lists only today's unchecked tasks plus at most 3 overdue
Reply is a few lines, no full-week dump
